clauses.text:
# order: EO:2122  (WPA 1944: 1915 Jan 20)
# WPA summary: Newton C. Llewellyn, former substitute carrier,made eligiblefor reinstatement as a carrierin the Knoxville, Tenn., post office without regard to length of separation from the service. 1915 CSR 121.
# book: Thirty-second Annual Report of the United States Civil Service Commission, fiscal year ended June 30, 1915
# scanned image 128, printed page 121; page lines 34-44
# source: https://archive.org/download/annualreportuni01commgoog/annualreportuni01commgoog_djvu.xml  sha256 92d8549007f776879ba70597db655a8e2deb53a49329d0574b35f0591c6fb041
# found by: monthday_and_names; date 1915-01-20; words newton|llewellyn|knoxville|tenn
# Government printed copy (OCR of a compilation or report), not the signed original. A lead for the
# original_text step: read it against the scan before use. Exact slice of the page OCR follows.
----- EXACT SLICE -----
has expired.
This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of War and the Chief
of Engineers, with the concurrence of the Civil Service Commission.
January 20, 1015.
Mr. Newton C. Llewellyn maybe reinstated as a carrier in the Knoxville, Tenn.,
post office without regard to the length of his separation from the service.
Mr. Llewellyn entered the Postal Service as a substitute carrier at Knoxville on
January 18, 1895, and remained in the service until February 28, 1907, when he
resigned.
The Postmaster General states that Mr. Llewellyn's record is good, that it is a
meritorious case, and that the department has no objection to the issuance of an order.
